newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Treatt cautious about current yr.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Treatt cautious about current yr.

text.p: Flavourings and fragrances supplier Treatt Plc said on Monday that it continued to be cautious about the outlook for the current financial year, but was confident about its long-term prospects.

Earlier Treatt, which provides more than 2,500 different products to the pharmaceutical and detergent industries as well as food and drink manufacturers, announced a 57 percent drop in full-year pre-tax profits to 1.52 million stg.
Shares in Treatt, which have dropped from a 12-month closing peak of 370 pence, dropped another 10 percent in mid-morning trade, falling 17 pence to a 12-month low of 153 pence.

Analysts had been forecasting pre-tax profit of around 2.0 million stg. Treatt blamed most of the profit fall on a sharp drop in prices for orange oil, used in a range of products from soft drinks to cleaning solvents, which it said had dropped "at a rate never before experienced."

Managing director Hugo Bovill told Reuters in a telephone interview that destocking, particularly by food manufacturers, also added to difficulties, while a relatively poor summer in northern Europe and the U.S. hit consumption of seasonal items such as drinks and ice creams.
Treatt said it was "most unlikely" to suffer from further steep falls in orange oil prices or other raw material price fluctuations, but added "we have to be cautious about prospects for this year."

Bovill said the first quarter of the current financial year to the end of September had continued to be difficult, with destocking and industry consolidation continuing at a similar pace. But he added: "We have a healthy order book. It is better than it was at the end of September". Treatt had moved "closer to normal trading levels," he added.

The group's Florida Treatt unit, which buys orange juice products in Florida and Brazil and produces concentrates to improve the taste of orange juice, was hardest hit by the downturn in orange oil prices.
Bovill said Treatt had acted to diversify Florida Treatt's operations, including moving into the processing of cucumbers.

The managing director said he remained confident about prospects for the longer term. "The industry has been growing for some number of years. We still believe that this is a growth industry - people will continue to eat and drink more and wash their clothes more," Bovill said.
